## Recommended minimal coherent scopes and ownership

Keep requirements with multiple layers under ONE primary owner, while named consumer tickets supply particular predicates. An early technical ticket can finish only its explicit D/E slice; the whole REQ stays incomplete until its P/R dependency resolves. If the build workflow requires closing that ticket, open exactly one owned pending-predicate deferral with owner/trigger/withheld claim, or make the late evidence/readout ticket the primary owner and classify the technical work as contributing evidence. Do not invent a second primary owner. Choosing the latter often produces a cleaner requirement index, but the former is valid with explicit owed accounting.

The following set is deliberately smaller than one ticket per REQ and avoids combining distinct long-running operator stages. Sizes are estimated total *read/reason/verify working set*, not changed LOC or calendar promises; reconfirm against actual worker context and keep well below half. Changed-line budgets are secondary proxies.

1. **TOOL: retained supplemental guard + actual native dispatch integration.** Full tooling contract, separate explicit implementation authorization before it may run; no product/runtime edits. Primary: REQ-H-001/002/003/005/006/007/008/011 and REQ-C-104/107/108. Own one versioned reader over existing records, scoped historical compatibility and actual selected native coordination invocation with stub workers. H-004 is owned by amendment/admission work; H-010 by methods/admission; H-009 by closure. Outputs are not a second machine state. ~22–30k tokens, ~600–1000 changed lines excluding fixtures; if integration cannot fit, split guard parser/fixtures then dispatch integration, with H-008 solely in latter and other ownership kept explicit. This is the only plausible bootstrap exception: guard implementation must be separately authorized and reviewed before product dispatch, not dispatched through the not-yet-built product guard. Planning documents cannot certify this obligation.

2. **CLI: selected boundary request repairs.** Full deterministic engineering contract. Primary: REQ-A-002, REQ-A-202. Repair only selected claim/launch/settle and comparison operands/forwarding, or consistently supply the supported restricted recipe; no CLI semantics, general RPC interface or new dependency. Input contract stays in hh-embed/1 owner. Consumers: offline lesson, reader journey, C-003 receipt prerequisite. ~10–16k tokens, 300–500 changed lines. AC-7-1 E: actual CLI→service tests traverse required fields and persist outcomes; old baseline fails. Recording method names alone is insufficient.

3. **OFFLINE: canonical EX-01/EX-02 recipes and semantic checks.** Full engineering contract after native receipt/R0 and *early* admitted analysis dependencies. Primary: REQ-A-008, REQ-F-102/103/104/105 (all four-family predicates explicitly consume later task/operations recipe evidence; do not close whole-family acceptance prematurely). Own common tiny canonical input/assertion/card format under scripts/examples and exact 20-subject offline lesson; EX-01 six fixture excerpts/R0/replay and no-provider route. Owning crates keep codecs; scripts compose. ~22–30k tokens, 600–900 changed lines. If parent chooses primary F-102/104/105 in later suite integration, OFFLINE is their E contributor only. Required sequence: 2 tasks ×2 arms ×5, task1 A=1/5 B=4/5; task2 A=3/5 B=2/5, real register/expand/open/next/claim/launch/settle/close, row and persisted/recomputed report joins; same inputs preserve report identity, one observation edit changes result. Controls: missing spec/row, bad lease, incompatible arm, duplicate settlement, binary/schema mismatch, tamper/missing/lifecycle mismatch, altered excerpt. All-success/all-failure binary cells retain valid uncertainty; undefined estimators alone refuse. Fixture evidence cannot close S1/S3. Analysis admission precedes this ticket but does not wait for paid parity/collection.

Scope: stable guides + three specified new pages, actual six-event annotated useful-task trace, EX-03 consumed cap/permission edit retained as new attempt/config, EX-04 links to all O1–O8×3 evidence. No invented ordering or action.effect.decided; do not relabel hh.submit fixture as real task. AC-7-1/2 D/E, AC-6-2 consumer, AC-5-1 consumer; A-201 and G-001/003/005 P predicates remain explicit shared participant dependencies. ~18–26k tokens, 600–1000 changed lines. To allow useful early documentation, the same contract may be a full D/E structural guide ticket with unavailable cards and a separately owned post-gate evidence-consumption closeout; it MUST NOT claim advertised exact recipes work until actual evidence exists. Verified external grammar at build-memory checker :379: `((HUMAN-H|GATE-G)[0-9]+|GATE-ACCEPT|[A-Z]+[0-9]*[a-z]?(\.[0-9]+[a-z]?)?)`, filenames 2–3 digits optional suffix. Existing gates go at least through GATE-G7 and HUMAN-H7; parent must enumerate actual full IDs and validate uniqueness. A fresh GATE-Gn is operator-acceptance role; never reuse GATE-ACCEPT identity/signature. Preserve current warning baseline, old files and exact legacy records.

Role map: CAP.1 independent all-scope gap hunt; CAP.2 composed execution→graded projection→analysis→recipient procedures and actual negative controls; CAP.3 closure/two sums/unique owed homes/all D/E/R/P completion limits; fresh GATE-G acceptance with exact words UTC/channel/items/expiry/void terms and draft-hash confirmation; REC.1 backlog/readiness with current artifact access/service evidence; REC.2 landed code/ADRs/coverage reconciliation; REC.3 actual stack CI/branches/release conditions; DOC.1 final reader/evidence/example refresh; DOC.2 agent ownership/verification guidance. Tail consumer audits do not duplicate primary REQ ownership. All reports get new round-specific paths; do not overwrite historical CAPSTONE/COMPOSED reports merely because templates use those names. REC read decisions belong explicitly under Decomposition decisions. Pending operator gate is RETURN PASS, technical failed prerequisite blockedOn; neither is permission to dispatch.

Gate/human graph: tool implementation authorization→TOOL→fresh readiness gate before products; semantics/method ADR admission before affected implementation; task/backend/model/oracle/environment/resource gate before any actual subject; rights/access/full-archive quote before distribution/retention; ready recipient procedures→actual outside invitation/consent/installation HUMAN→outside readout→formative authorization/HUMAN→formative report and severe-defect repair→capability-publication GATE/HUMAN→manual day30/day90 HUMAN/value report. Exact recipient dates/rights/host/contact/quote and real native records are outstanding action inputs; absence prevents dependent execution, not all independent offline engineering.

## What needs authoritative input versus implementation judgment

Missing authoritative: actual task/runner/image/oracle/model/supported backend and finite execution exposure; independent method/contract admission, signed dimensions/margins and numerical gates; actual rights/retention/access host/contact/dates/full archive quote; selected optional consumer/version/format/provisioning; actual outside identity/install/signer/consent/invitation authority; cohort/rubric-scoring assignments and publication/deletion dates; capability/scientific publication decisions; fresh round acceptance words. Use HUMAN/GATE + post-gate skeletons, never guesses. New backend/public API/dependency/tier/contract/resource expansion needs explicit design/admission.

Routine: exact private script/module name, tiny fixture ordering that meets pinned totals, selected existing supported cap field after tracing enforcement, docs structure within three approved pages, error display plumbing, packaging harness composition over existing Rust APIs, test names, internal observer-record formatting. These do not justify a blanket return to design. Frozen spec already gives enough design to author full TOOL, CLI, offline lesson, CI, contribution and preparatory D contracts. The planned guard's private script path can be chosen by the owning tooling contract; it is not missing product architecture.
